pr_body:
We implemented CREATE SCHEMA in declarative schema changer.

We fallback when AUTHORIZATION clause is specified since we support
user-related management in declarative schema changer.

Fix #103200
Epic: [CRDB-27883](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-27883)
Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/102364)
What purpose does this `SchemaName` element serve? Why couldn't `Namespace` be used?

> What purpose does this `SchemaName` element serve? Why couldn't `Namespace` be used?

IIRC that it's used to set the name within the descriptor itself. We could have used Namespace, but then we'd need to do 2 things within one op (write namespace row + set name of the descriptor).

I see. Still, the name in the descriptor and the name in the namespace table need to remain in sync at all times (not to mention the backreference in the db and whatnot). Do we have rules to ensure that these name elements all always transition in the same stage?

I'm not fundamentally opposed but I'm not convinced that the implications of this scheme have been properly thought out.
mhm...that's a good call. I don't think we added rules to enforce the invariant :(

I haven't investigated further but perhaps `BEGIN; CREATE SCHEMA sc; DROP SCHEMA sc; COMMIT` would be worth testing to exercise things a bit more. Also, shouldn't `SchemaName` be produced by `scdecomp`? 

I'm very tempted to revert this PR right now.

issue_context.title: schemachanger: Implement CREATE SCHEMA
issue_context.body:
As a prerequisite of supporting CREATE DATABASE in the declarative schema changer, we need to support CREATE SCHEMA first.

Jira issue: CRDB-27883


Epic CRDB-31331

review_comments: while you're here, could you also add a commit to add eventlog for CREATE FUNCTION? thanks!

instead of adding `addedNames` field here, can we use `newDescriptors` instead? I suppose we can get same information from them and creating new descriptors normally means we need to add new names except for Functions. That being said, I'm fine with your approach, but just prefer to avoid adding new fields if possible.
